judged_text: Pagination race in admin-group next/previous: each click computes offset from current model state and fires an unguarded findMembers whose response overwrites offset, user_count, and members in completion order; rapid clicks can issue duplicate requests (model offset isn't updated until the response arrives) and out-of-order responses leave the UI showing a page other than the one last clicked

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next`/`previous` actions update `group.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` without canceling/serializing in-flight requests. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` issues an AJAX request and then `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response (`result.meta.*`). If multiple clicks trigger multiple `findMembers()` calls, responses can resolve out of order and an older response will overwrite `members` and `offset` to an earlier page, leaving the UI showing a page other than the last click. (The finding’s sub-claim that offset isn’t updated until the response arrives is incorrect, since `group.set("offset", offset)` happens before the request, but the out-of-order overwrite is still real.)
